answer:
**Raise prices and tighten booking now; wait on the second van.** With hiring taking two months, buying on October 19 leaves little operating time to increase this year’s profit.

Using 26 operating days per month, you complete 156 grooms. Each currently contributes $45 after groomer pay and supplies/fuel: $95 × 60% − $12. That produces **$3,220 monthly operating profit** after $3,800 fixed costs, before tax, owner compensation and unlisted expenses.

Over the next 90 days:

- **Charge new customers $115 immediately.** Give regulars 30 days’ notice of a $105 rate, honoring already quoted appointments. Keep this regular-client preference through the trial.
- **Offer regulars recurring appointments six to eight weeks ahead.** Hold capacity according to their actual rebooking needs; release unused slots to the waitlist.
- **Group appointments geographically**, use reminders and a clear cancellation policy, and contact a route-specific waitlist when openings appear.

At a 70% regular/30% new mix, the average ticket becomes $108. Contribution rises to $52.80 per groom, producing **$4,437 monthly profit—$1,217 more** once fully implemented. About 133 monthly grooms would preserve today’s profit, giving roughly 15% volume headroom.

The second van deserves reconsideration after 30–45 days of testing prices and validating demand. Fifteen additional weekly grooms at $115 would contribute approximately $3,705 monthly; subtracting financing leaves **$2,055 before additional insurance, maintenance, software and staffing costs**. Those requests represent only 42% of another van’s capacity.

Proceed when customers accept the higher price, requests convert into recurring bookings in workable routes, and contribution covers all incremental costs plus a cash reserve. Begin recruiting research now, but commit to financing only after that validation.
